query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization can increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases
generation.intervention: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching
generation.conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
generation.mechanism: The local von Mises strain in the FCC phase can be up to 6 times higher than that in the B2 phase during deformation, leading to improved strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa
generation.baseline: As-cast alloy with ∼14% fracture true strain and ∼1390 MPa fracture true stress
generation.boundary: The phase-selective recrystallization process may not be effective for all types of eutectic high-entropy alloys or under different testing conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms by which phase-selective recrystallization improves strength and ductility are not fully understood and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without phase-selective recrystallization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the phase-selectively recrystallized alloy does not show significant improvements in strength and ductility compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement.
